summary: The root دخر (dkhr) describes being object, mean, contemptible, or despicable. It implies a state of lowliness or abasement.
lane: 1 دَخَرَ دخر , (S, A, Msb, K,) aor. دَخَرَ ; (Msb, K;) and دَخِرَ , aor. دَخَرَ ; (K;) inf. n. of the former, دُخُورٌ , (S, A, Msb, K,) and (of the latter, TA) دَخَرٌ ; (K, TA; in the CK دُخْرٌ ;) He was, or became, object, mean, contemptible, or despicable. (S, A, Msb, K.)

ادخرهُ أدخره ادخره ادخرة ٱدخر ٱدخره He (God, A, or a man, Msb) rendered him abject, mean, contemptible, or despicable. (S, A, Msb, K.)
ادّخر أدخر ادخر ٱدخر: see art. خر.
دَاخِرٌ داخر, applied to a man, Abject, mean, contemptible, or despicable. (S, TA.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
